text: The NJROTC uniform is worn by all cadets at least one full school day each week and on other occasions the naval science instructor prescribes.
q: How often must cadets wear the NJROTC uniform at minimum?
a: One full school day each week

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L

text: Uniform articles of sister services are not authorized with the NJROTC uniform.
q: Which uniform articles are not authorized with the NJROTC uniform?
distractors: The black V-neck Navy pullover (SWO) sweater
Cargo pants with a unit tee shirt for field activities

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L

text: Outdoors, cadets stay covered at all times except when ordered to uncover or during religious services not tied to a military ceremony.
q: When outdoors in uniform, when may a cadet be uncovered?
a: When ordered to uncover, or at religious services not part of a military ceremony
distractors: Whenever standing in a formation at ease
Whenever the cadet is on school grounds

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Cadets must be in a complete uniform that meets the standards whenever they are in uniform; a partial uniform worn to preserve it for inspection is not permitted.
q: What state of uniform must a cadet be in whenever in uniform, including in other school classes?
distractors: Complete only during drill and ceremonies

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: When worn, the name tag is on the right side of the uniform, opposite the ribbons, with its bottom aligned with the bottom row of ribbons.
q: On which side of the uniform is the name tag worn?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Uniformed cadets may not take part in political activities, private employment, or commercial interests that imply official sponsorship.
q: Which activities may a cadet in uniform not take part in?
a: Political activities, private employment, or commercial interests implying official sponsorship
distractors: Field meets in the prescribed uniform
Parades the naval science instructor prescribes

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Male sideburns are neatly trimmed, of even width, and do not extend below a point level with the middle of the ear.
q: How far down may male cadet sideburns extend?
a: No lower than level with the middle of the ear
distractors: To the bottom of the earlobe
To the corner of the mouth

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: A male mustache must be neat and closely trimmed, must not extend below the upper lip line, and must not extend more than 1/4 inch beyond a vertical line from the corners of the mouth; no other facial hair is permitted.
q: How far beyond a vertical line from the corners of the mouth may a male cadet's mustache extend?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Fingernails must not extend past the fingertips.
q: How long may a male cadet's fingernails be?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: One ring per hand is authorized, and one wristwatch and one bracelet; ankle bracelets are not.
q: How many rings are authorized per hand?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Necklaces are authorized but must not be visible.
q: How must a necklace be worn with the NJROTC uniform?
a: So that it is not visible
distractors: Tucked so only the chain shows

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Sunglasses are never authorized in military formations.
q: When are sunglasses authorized in military formations?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Women's hair in uniform may touch, but not fall below, a horizontal line level with the lower edge of the back of the collar.
q: How long may a female cadet's hair be in uniform?
a: It may touch but not fall below the lower edge of the back of the collar
distractors: Down to the middle of the back

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: When bangs are worn, they must not extend below the eyebrows.
q: How far may female cadet bangs extend?
distractors: To the top of the nose
To the middle of the cheek

source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: Hair bulk, minus the bun, may not exceed 2 inches from the scalp, and the bun may not exceed 3 inches from the scalp.
q: What is the maximum bun bulk measured from the scalp?

text: The NJROTC patch is worn on the left sleeve of the short sleeve khaki shirt, the Service Dress Blue coat, and the black relaxed fit jacket, with its top edge 1 inch below the shoulder seam.
q: On which sleeve is the NJROTC patch worn?
distractors: Neither; it is worn on the chest

source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: The NJROTC patch is not worn on the raincoat, peacoat, all-weather coat, parka, or the long sleeve white shirt with Service Dress Blue.
q: On which garment is the NJROTC patch NOT worn?

text: Service stars are five-pointed gold stars that show courses or years completed, centered 1/4 inch above the left breast pocket or the ribbons.
q: What do NJROTC service stars indicate?
a: Courses or years satisfactorily completed in the program

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: A service star is a metal five-pointed gold device 3/8 inch diagonally across, spaced 1/4 inch apart when more than one is worn.
q: How far apart are multiple service stars spaced?

source.title: NJROTC Cadet Field Manual (CFM), 12th Edition, NAVEDTRA 37116-L
source.publisher: Naval Service Training Command (NSTC), U.S. Navy

text: The JROTC device is worn on the left collar and the rank or rate device on the right collar.
q: Which collar carries the rank or rate device?
distractors: Neither; it is worn on the sleeve

text: A fouled anchor is worn on the left side of the garrison cap by all cadets; cadet officers and chiefs wear rank/rate insignia on the right side.
